---
title: "020 — Branch back-propagation"
---

> **Status:** standing (merged to main 2026-09-06 via PR #32; not yet in a tagged release
> at the time of writing)

**Goal.** Let branched chats push their outcomes back into the parent chat's context as
user-controlled, anchored, collapsible artifacts, so the parent stops silently trusting
stale assumptions — it still believed code it produced was correct after the user fixed it
on a branch, so resuming the parent answered from a version of reality the user had
already moved past. The idea→spec relationship is direct: ideas/008-branch-context-sync
seeded this spec, its verdict choosing Card 001's back-propagation refined through
playthrough into a new, anchored, collapsible entry kind on the existing `messages` table
— no new persistence paradigm — with two payload modes (the verbatim raw branch delta, or
a model-written summary), anchored exactly at the branch point, purely additive, never
history-altering.

**Why.** Branching exists to step aside and fix something; the fix lived only on the
branch. The idea stage's rejected cards define the design by negation: plain sync notes
carry no authority over the parent's earlier confident claims; divergence-marker detection
needs an LLM pass per branch ("bad idea, very expensive"); branch promotion alters
history ("I don't like history altering"); a tree-scoped decision ledger charges a
separate store plus a per-turn relevance cost. The idea's codebase research settled the
winner: the message kind model from [#002](#sec-002) already provides persisted, ordered,
collapsible entries — the artifact only needed to become a new kind.

**Outcome & reversals.** Merged through PR #32 and user-verified end to end. The
implementation rides existing abstractions throughout: the anchor reuses
`chats.branch_point_message_id`, with composer-created branches that lack a fork point
deriving one from creation time and labeling it `derived`; the raw delta needs no diffing
because branch chats copy zero messages — every branch row rendered verbatim *is* the
delta; the row stores `role: 'user'` and stays out of both provider-exclusion sets, so it
steers every future composition as real history rather than overlay, while sibling
branches stay isolated by the existing cutoff-inclusive ancestor walk. The one schema
change — `messages.ord` from integer to double precision — buys mid-thread placement via
midpoint insert with no rebalancing path, and none may ever be added, because propagation
never rewrites existing rows. Two reversals landed inside the PR, both caught in user
testing: summary generation initially carried its instructions only in the system prompt,
so a branch ending on a large assistant reply made the call read as "continue the
transcript" and emit lesson content instead of a handoff summary — fixed by anchoring the
summary task as a trailing user turn; and the summary's word cap was dropped in favor of a
relevance budget, on the ruling that maximal factual detail (a corrected snippet of
syntax, say) may be exactly what the parent needs — only exploratory narration is dropped.
The load-bearing data-model contract — artifact row shape, metadata, ord placement,
composition mapping — is preserved verbatim at
[appendices/020-branch-backprop-data-model.md](appendices/020-branch-backprop-data-model.md).

**Learnings.**

- A new entry kind follows the adoption checklist — type unions, lane, render case,
  projection case, search filter; an unhandled kind silently vanishes from LLM context.
- Fractional ordering buys insertion without rewriting: make rewriting impossible, not
  merely avoided.
- Authority is a design property: a structured, anchored artifact steers the parent;
  plain prose merely hopes to.
- Steering works by being real history — a user-role row in the parent's transcript —
  not by an injection mechanism beside it.
